clue.text: Chap has one boat refurbished in Canada

parts.note: a chap is a man
the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: something refurbished is done up and remade, so these letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A man with a done-up boat sets off somewhere in Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in Canada' defines a place there; 'refurbished' makes TOBA from the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Manitoba is one of the prairie provinces, so it is a place found in Canada.

clue.text: Up-to-date sailors get under way

indicators.note: get under places the sailors below the next word in this down entry

parts.note: a mode is a way or manner
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Modern seamen start their voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up-to-date' looks like a description of the sailors, but it is the definition; 'get under' only works because this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Modern means current, belonging to the present.

clue.text: A plant to cause irritation

explanation.definitionFit: The nettle is a stinging weed, and to nettle is to annoy.

clue.text: A principle that is not irreversible

indicators.note: not irreversible means the word reads the same backwards as forwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A belief that can be undone.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a doctrine or belief held as true.

clue.text: A page, however, has plenty

parts.note: however means but
tons means plenty, lots

explanation.surface: A pageboy who has lots nonetheless.
explanation.walkthrough: Buttons is the traditional name for a hotel pageboy, from his buttoned uniform; also a pantomime character.
explanation.definitionFit: Buttons is a nickname for a uniformed boy servant or bellboy.

clue.text: Elderly alumnus returned from the wine-shop

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the run of letters for these two words is read from the end

parts.note: elderly means aged
an alumnus is an old boy, abbreviated OB

explanation.surface: An aged former pupil comes home from the off-licence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns AGEDOB around to give BODEGA. OB (old boy) is a British term for a former pupil of a school.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodega is a Spanish wine cellar or shop selling wine.

clue.text: Tell me if it's not in vogue and trendy!

parts.note: something not fashionable is out
with it means trendy, up to date

explanation.surface: Asking whether something is unfashionable and fashionable at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Out with it is an urging to speak up and say what is on one's mind.

clue.text: Model finds former MP in real distress

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: in means the MP goes inside the rearranged letters
distress means damage, so the letters of real are put in disorder

explanation.surface: An ex-politician is found in genuine trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like a fashion model but is the definition; 'distress' makes ELAR, which 'in' wraps round MP.
explanation.definitionFit: An exemplar is a model or example to follow.

clue.text: Posture reveals one's way of thinking

definitions.meaning: a stance or pose of the body

explanation.definitionFit: Attitude means both a bodily stance and a settled mental outlook.

clue.text: Mark came back in time to set off

indicators.note: in means the reversed piece goes inside the word for time

parts.note: a date is a time

indicators.note: came back means the word for mark is written backwards

parts.note: to mark something is to note it

explanation.surface: A grade was returned just in time for something to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a verb, but it is a noun meaning a note; 'came back' gives ETON and 'in' places it within the time word.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off a bomb is to make it explode.

clue.text: Testify that a sober man is in Paris

parts.note: TT stands for teetotal, a sober abstainer
est is French for is

explanation.surface: A man of temperance gives evidence about being in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to bear witness or declare something true under oath.

clue.text: Way to upset a king and emperor

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned over, so the letters for way are reversed

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
R is short for rex, king

explanation.surface: A path that overturns both a monarch and an emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar was the ruler of Russia, with the rank of emperor.

clue.text: Dealings with a variety of Orientals

indicators.note: a variety is a mixture of forms, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Trade carried on with all sorts of people from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Relations between parties are their dealings or contacts with each other.

clue.text: One Pole set to make a contribution

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
N is the north pole
to set something down is to put it

explanation.surface: A Polish person is ready to chip in.
explanation.definitionFit: Input is what someone adds to a joint effort, their share of ideas or work.

clue.text: Proceed to get a warrant

definitions.meaning: to proceed is to go on or move past
a warrant here is a permit allowing someone through

explanation.definitionFit: Pass means to go by and also a permit authorising entry.

clue.text: Dispute makes old German create trouble

parts.note: alt is German for old

indicators.note: trouble means to disturb, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: An argument where an elderly German causes bother.
explanation.definitionFit: To altercate is to quarrel or argue heatedly.

clue.text: Tried again to read her composition

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so these letters are arranged anew

explanation.surface: A case was retried so that she could read out her essay.
explanation.definitionFit: A case reheard in court has been tried a second time.

clue.text: Companion entered earlier for a glass of sherry

indicators.note: entered means one piece has gone inside the other

parts.note: sooner means earlier
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A friend arrived ahead of time for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entered' signals insertion; a schooner in Britain is a large sherry glass, not only a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A schooner is a tall glass used for sherry in Britain.

clue.text: Hesitated to get francs changed

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for francs
altered means changed

explanation.surface: Someone paused before exchanging currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Faltered means wavered or paused unsteadily.

clue.text: Gossip about Lewis's madman

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
the Mad Hatter is a character in Lewis Carroll's Alice in Wonderland

explanation.surface: Talk about the lunatic in a Lewis Carroll story.
explanation.definitionFit: Chatter is idle talk, the same as gossip.

clue.text: Strain to build a stack

definitions.meaning: to wrench or sprain a joint
a haystack or pile of hay

explanation.definitionFit: Rick means both a sprain and a stack of hay.

clue.text: Little fellow consumed the lot

parts.note: F is the short form of fellow
consumed means ate

explanation.surface: A small man has eaten everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Fate is one's destiny, one's lot in life.

clue.text: Crooked dealer harbours top-quality earthenware

indicators.note: harbours means holds inside, so one piece shelters another

parts.note: a fence deals in stolen goods
A1 means top quality, written with I for 1

explanation.surface: A dishonest trader hides first-rate pottery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'harbours' signals holding inside; a fence is a receiver of stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Faience is glazed pottery.

clue.text: Recess in a large cavern

parts.note: a cove is a sheltered hollow or small cave

explanation.surface: A nook within a big cave.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcove is a recessed part of a room.

clue.text: Benefit from bespoke tailoring?

definitions.meaning: made-to-measure clothing gives a professional fit

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the answer as PRO FIT, the fit a professional tailor gives.
explanation.definitionFit: Profit is gain or advantage.

clue.text: Creature featured in Beatrix Potter's books

indicators.note: featured in means the answer sits within the words that follow

explanation.surface: An animal appears in the children's books of Beatrix Potter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'featured in' points to the run inside 'Potter's'.
explanation.definitionFit: An otter is a water-loving animal of the weasel family.

clue.text: Sculptor offers Greek cross to vendor

parts.note: the Greek letter chi is written as a cross, X
a vendor is a seller

explanation.surface: An artist sells a Greek cross to a trader.
explanation.definitionFit: A chiseller works stone or wood with a chisel, as a carver does.

clue.text: Compère awarded the MC

definitions.meaning: the letters M and C spelt out as words

explanation.definitionFit: Emcee is the host of a show, from the sound of the letters M C.

clue.text: Usual number going to Sandhurst? 50

parts.note: Sandhurst is the Royal Military Academy, RMA
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A typical intake of fifty cadets at the army college.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandhurst is the British army's officer training academy.
explanation.definitionFit: Normal means ordinary, the standard state of things.

clue.text: Rob has to leave work

definitions.meaning: to rob is to steal, slang for knocking something off
to stop working for the day, end the shift

explanation.definitionFit: Knock off is slang both for stealing and for finishing work.

clue.text: Blush when shown Socialist study

parts.note: a red is a left-winger or socialist
a den is a private study room

explanation.surface: Someone colours up when the left-winger is seen in their study.
explanation.definitionFit: To redden is to turn pink in the face from embarrassment.

clue.text: Forceful, muscular fellows confined by surgeon

indicators.note: confined by means one piece is held inside another

parts.note: a vet is a veterinary surgeon
he-men are strong, muscle-bound men

explanation.surface: Powerful bodybuilders are restrained by a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confined by' signals holding inside; 'surgeon' suggests a hospital doctor but means an animal doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehement means intense and passionate in force.
